domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's leave application. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and potential cancellation. References the employee, the leave type (policy), and the approving/rejecting/cancelling actor.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific leave type within a fiscal year. Deducted when a leave request is approved; restored when an approved leave is cancelled. Each (employee, leaveType, fiscalYear) tuple is unique.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organisation. Holds identity, reporting-line (managerId), and employment lifecycle state. Employment status gates all leave operations — only ACTIVE employees may submit leave requests.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Governs how many days an employee is entitled to, whether manager approval is required, minimum notice periods, and accrual behaviour. Referenced by LeaveBalance to determine entitlements and by LeaveRequest to validate compliance.

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Represents a notification sent to a user (employee or manager) in response to leave-related events: request submitted, approved, rejected, or cancelled. Links back to the originating entity for traceability.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type may be governed by a distinct LeavePolicy. The feature scope covers annual, sick, and emergency; unpaid, maternity, and paternity are defined for completeness.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of states a LeaveRequest can occupy. Drives the leave request lifecycle state machine. Transitions: DRAFT→SUBMITTED, DRAFT→CANCELLED, SUBMITTED→APPROVED, SUBMITTED→REJECTED, SUBMITTED→CANCELLED, APPROVED→CANCELLED. REJECTED is terminal.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalanceStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of states a LeaveBalance can occupy. Transitions: ACTIVE→EXHAUSTED (remainingDays hits 0), EXHAUSTED→ACTIVE (balance restored via cancellation), ACTIVE→FROZEN (admin action), FROZEN→ACTIVE (admin unfreeze), ACTIVE→CLOSED (fiscal year end), EXHAUSTED→CLOSED (fiscal year end), FROZEN→CLOSED (fiscal year end). CLOSED is terminal.

domain_entities.name: EmploymentStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of employment states. Gates all leave operations. Transitions: ACTIVE→INACTIVE (suspension/extended leave), INACTIVE→ACTIVE (reinstatement), ACTIVE→TERMINATED (employment ends), INACTIVE→TERMINATED (termination while inactive). TERMINATED is terminal.

domain_entities.name: NotificationType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of notification categories triggered by leave lifecycle events. Each type maps to a specific domain event and determines the notification template and routing.

modules.name: leave-type
owns: LeaveType enum (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity)

modules.name: leave-request-status
owns: LeaveRequestStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED)

modules.name: leave-policy
owns: LeavePolicy model (id, policyName, leaveType, entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt)

modules.name: employee
owns: Employee model (id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, managerId, department, hireDate, terminationDate, employmentStatus, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt)

modules.name: leave-request
owns: LeaveRequest model (id, employeeId, leaveTypeId, startDate, endDate, reason, status, approvedBy, approvedAt, rejectedBy, rejectedAt, rejectionReason, cancelledBy, cancelledAt, cancellationReason, createdAt, updatedAt)

sql_schemas: table leave_types | fields: id, name, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: name: unique lookup by leave type name (e.g. 'annual', 'sick', 'emergency') — used in every leave request creation and policy resolution path; is_active: filters active leave types for dropdowns and policy assignment screens

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: join path when resolving which policy applies to a leave request; also used in balance calculations; is_active: filters active policies for employee-facing leave type listings and HR configuration screens

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number — used in every employee resolution path; email: unique lookup for login and notification delivery; manager_id: 'my direct reports' queries for manager approval workflows and team views; department: HR filtering and departmental leave calendar views; employment_status: filters active employees for leave eligibility checks

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, rejected_by, rejected_at, rejection_reason, cancelled_by, cancelled_at, cancellation_reason, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id; rejected_by -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: primary access pattern — employees list their own leave requests; also used in manager team views; status: filters by status (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED) for approval queues and dashboards; leave_type_id: filters by leave type for reporting and balance reconciliation; start_date: range queries for calendar views and overlapping-request detection; end_date: range queries for calendar views and overlapping-request detection; approved_by: lookup for audit trails showing who approved what; rejected_by: lookup for audit trails showing who rejected what

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, leave_type_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: employee_id: primary access pattern — employees check their own balances; also used in leave-request validation to check remaining days; policy_id: join path for policy resolution and HR balance reports grouped by policy; fiscal_year: filters balances to the current fiscal year; combined with employee_id for the most frequent query shape; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint index — one balance row per employee per policy per fiscal year; also the lookup key during leave request validation; leave_type_id: denormalized fast path for balance lookups by leave type without joining through policy

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: primary access pattern — fetch all notifications for a given user; status: filters unread/read/archived notifications for inbox views; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: trace back from notification to the originating leave request or balance event; created_at: chronological ordering for notification feeds

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: primary access pattern — 'show me all changes to leave request X' or 'all changes to employee Y'; action: filters by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE) for compliance reports; performed_by: 'who did what' queries for audit review; performed_at: time-range queries for audit log browsing and retention policies
